genesis_at_a_glance.1: This book records the creation of all things, the fall of man, the universal flood and the Tower of Babel. It also overviews the lives of four all-important Old Testament individuals, namely, Abraham, his son Isaac, one of Isaac’s two sons, Jacob, and one of Jacob’s 12 sons, Joseph.

bottom_line_introduction.1: AMAZING INDEED! THE WHEN, WHO, HOW, AND WHAT OF ALL THINGS EXPLAINED IN TEN SHORT WORDS!
bottom_line_introduction.d: The heavens and the earth (the what)

facts_regarding_the_author_of_this_book.1: Who? Moses. He was the younger brother of Aaron and Miriam (Ex. 6:20; Num. 26:59) who led his people Israel out of Egyptian bondage (Ex. 5-14) and gave them the law of God at Mt. Sinai (Exodus 20).
facts_regarding_the_author_of_this_book.2: What? The books of Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, and Deuteronomy.
facts_regarding_the_author_of_this_book.3: When and where? 1405 B.C., from the eastern bank of the River Jordan in Moab.
facts_regarding_the_author_of_this_book.5: To whom? Israel in particular, all believers in general.

4: Why?.a: Genesis. To record the origin of the world and the nation Israel.
4: Why?.b: Exodus. The supernatural deliverance of Israel from Egyptian bondage.
4: Why?.c: Leviticus. The purpose and functions of the tabernacle.
4: Why?.d: Numbers. The failure of Israel to enter Canaan.
4: Why?.e: Deuteronomy. The review of the Law for that generation about to enter Canaan.

key_events.4: The births of Cain and Abel
key_events.9: The giving of the Abrahamic Covenant
key_events.12: The marriage of Isaac and Rebekah
key_events.13: The births of Jacob and Esau
key_events.14: The marriage of Jacob to Leah and Rachel
key_events.15: The elevation of Joseph in Egypt
key_events.16: The move of Jacob and his family from Canaan to Egypt

key_individuals.1: Adam: First human, from whose side woman was taken
key_individuals.2: Eve: First woman and wife of Adam
key_individuals.3: Cain: First son of Adam and Eve, and first human to be born
key_individuals.4: Abel: Godly second son of Adam who was murdered by his brother Cain
key_individuals.5: Methuselah: World’s oldest human who died at the age of 969 years
key_individuals.6: Enoch: Father of Methuselah whom God removed from this earth without dying
key_individuals.7: Noah: The man God chose to build an Ark and save a remnant of humanity (Namely, his family) from a worldwide flood
key_individuals.8: Shem, Ham, and Japheth: Three sons of Noah from whom all human beings have sprung
key_individuals.9: Canaan: Wicked grandson (through Ham) who was guilty of an undisclosed sin against his grandfather, resulting in a curse.
key_individuals.10: Abraham: Father of the Nation Israel and the spiritual father of all believers
key_individuals.11: Sarah: Wife of Abraham and mother of Isaac
key_individuals.13: Hagar: Egyptian wife of Abraham and mother of Ishmael
key_individuals.14: Ishmael: Son of Hagar and Abraham and probably father of the Arab race
key_individuals.15: Isaac: The promised heir of Abraham and his barren wife Sarah
key_individuals.16: Rebekah: A relative of Abraham living in Mesopotamia who would become the wife of Isaac
key_individuals.17: Eliezer: Thought to be Abraham’s faithful servant who traveled to Mesopotamia and brought back Rebekah
key_individuals.18: Laban: Rachel’s father and later Isaac’s uncle
key_individuals.19: Jacob: Second born twin of Isaac and Rebekah
key_individuals.20: Esau: First born twin son of Isaac and Rebekah who would later sell his birthright to Jacob and eventually forfeit his blessing
key_individuals.21: Leah: Jacob’s first wife, who gave birth to six of his 12 sons and only recorded daughter
key_individuals.23: Rachel: Jacob’s second and most beloved wife
key_individuals.25: Potiphar’s wife: Wicked woman who falsely accused Joseph of rape, resulting in his imprisonment
key_individuals.26: Pharaoh: Egyptian king who placed Joseph over all the land after he had interpreted the ruler’s two dreams.

key_places.1: Garden of Eden: original home of Adam and Eve, probably located between the Tigris and Euphrates River
key_places.2: Land of Nod: Place where the rebel Cain fled after killing his brother Abel
key_places.3: Mt. Ararat: Mountain in Turkey where the Ark of Noah settled down
key_places.4: Land of Shinar: Place where the Tower of Babel was built, near where the city of Babylon would later be built
key_places.5: Ur of the Chaldees: Abraham’s original home, located near the Euphrates River
key_places.6: Bethel: Place where Abraham built his first altar upon reaching the land of Canaan
key_places.7: Egypt: Abraham backslid and went here during a famine in Canaan
key_places.8: Sodom: Wicked city located on the banks of the Dead Sea which was destroyed by God
key_places.9: Salem: Thought to be the first Mention of Jerusalem where Abraham met Melchizedek
key_places.10: Mt. Moriah: Elevated area near Jerusalem where Abraham offered up his son Isaac
key_places.11: Cave of Machpelah: Located south of Jerusalem where Abraham buried his wife Sarah
key_places.12: Jabbok: A tributary stream flowing into the Jordan river where Jacob wrestled with God
key_places.13: Bethlehem: Where Jacob buried his beloved wife Rachel
key_places.14: Land of Goshen: Area in Egypt where Jacob and his extended family settled

unique_features.1: Genesis spans a total time period of at least 2,200 years. In light of this, note God’s priority here. He employed 20 percent of the book (1-11) to describe the first 1,800 years. This covers Creation, the Fall, the flood, and Babel. He employed 80 percent of the book (12-50) to describe the final 400 years. Here we read of Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and Joseph. This means approximately 80 percent of the total time period is covered in only 11 chapters, while 20 percent of the time is described in 39 chapters. The priority point is simple—in the mind of God, Abraham is more important than the universe.
unique_features.2: It is the only book which describes God as resting (2:2, 3).
unique_features.3: It gives the first prophecy of the coming Messiah, of his suffering and eventual victory (3:15).
unique_features.4: It provides his first two names (Seed of the woman and Shiloh) (3:15; 49:10).
unique_features.5: It pin points the tribe from whence he would come (Judah) and is the first book to mention the city where he would be born (Bethlehem) . See 49:10; 35:19.
unique_features.6: It gives us the first human to be created (Adam) and the first human to be born (Cain) (1:26; 4:1).
unique_features.7: It records the first man to die (Abel) and the first man not to die (Enoch) (4:8; 5:24).
unique_features.8: The glory of God in creation (1:1) and the grace of God in salvation (Noah) (6:8) are both clearly seen.
unique_features.9: We see the world’s earliest civilization (Cainite) and the world’s oldest citizen (Methuselah) (4:17; 5:27).
unique_features.10: The first three of four divine institutions as found in Genesis:
unique_features.11: It provides the first illustration of human religion (the fig leaves), and the first example of divine redemption (the coats of skin) (3:7, 21).
unique_features.12: Here a city is destroyed on the plains (Sodom) and a boy is spared on a mountain (Isaac) (19, 22).
unique_features.13: Here a son (Jacob) deceives his father (Isaac) and is later himself deceived by his sons (brothers of Joseph) (27, 37).
unique_features.14: Here we read of the first barren mother (Sarah) and the first dying mother (Rachel) (16, 35).
unique_features.15: Jerusalem (a type of the heavenly) and Egypt (a type of the worldly) are first mentioned in this stage (13, 14).
unique_features.16: Here we first learn of a king called Melchizedek and a cave named Machpelah (14, 25).
unique_features.17: Here the first of three great biblical covenants is introduced (12:1-3). These covenants are:
unique_features.18: In its pages sinners are drowned, and a saint (Noah) is drunken (7:21, 9:20-21).
unique_features.19: A ship settles on a mountain and a tower rises on a plain (8:4, 11:1-4). This tower is but the beginning of three satanic attempts to consolidate religion around a project. Two more will follow. One was built near Babylon (Dan. 2), and the final one will be placed in the Holy of Holies (Rev. 13).
unique_features.20: History’s first rebellion (Babel) and revival (Bethel) occurred in this book (11:4; 35:2-4).
unique_features.21: Here Abraham climbs a mountain where God’s Lamb would someday die (22:2). On this occasion Isaac asks his father a question that would be answered by John the Baptist some 20 centuries later. The question asked by Isaac: “Where is the Lamb?” (22:7). The answer given by John: “Behold the Lamb of God, who taketh away the sin of the world” (John 1:29).

17: Here the first of three great biblic.a: The Abrahamic Covenant (12:1-3). This has to do with a land (Canaan) and a people (Israel).
17: Here the first of three great biblic.b: The Davidic Covenant (2 Sam. 7:4-16; 1 Chron. 17:3-5). This has to do with a king to rule in that land over that people.
17: Here the first of three great biblic.c: The New Covenant (Jer. 31:31). This has to do with changed hearts so that the people in the land will allow the king to rule over them.

comparison_with_other_bible_books.a: Genesis records humanity’s first rebellion against God (3:1-6); Revelation records the final rebellion (Rev. 20:7-10).
comparison_with_other_bible_books.b: Genesis records the entrance of sin (3:1-6); Revelation records its exit (Rev. 20:10; 21:4-8).
comparison_with_other_bible_books.c: Genesis records the imposition of the curse (3:9-19); Revelation records the lifting of the curse (Rev. 22:3).
comparison_with_other_bible_books.d: Genesis records the beginning of death (3:19); Revelation records the end of death (Rev. 21:4).
comparison_with_other_bible_books.e: Genesis records the creation of the present heavens and earth (1:1); Revelation records the creation of the new heavens and earth (Rev. 21:1).
comparison_with_other_bible_books.f: In Genesis, Abraham is the patriarch of Israel; in Romans, he is the patriarch of all who believe (Rom. 4:16).
comparison_with_other_bible_books.g: All “begin at the beginning,” but their beginnings are different: Genesis begins with Creation; John and 1 John begin before Creation, with the preexistent Word.
comparison_with_other_bible_books.h: Both show that salvation is by faith (15:6; Gal. 3:6).
comparison_with_other_bible_books.i: Both show God’s desire to redeem all humanity (12:2-3; Gal. 3:8).
